title: Root knot nematodes in outdoor tomatoes

Header: Root knot nematodes in outdoor tomatoes
Meloidogyne incognita , M. hapla , M. javanica “Minyoo fundo” in Swahili

Prevention: Transplant seedlings with healthy roots, free of nematodes.
Change seedbed location in next cropping season.
Rotate tomatoes every season with nematode-non-susceptible crops (e.g. sunhemp, cabbage, sorghum;).
French marigold ( Tagetes patula ) because its roots contain chemicals that kill nematodes.
Or intercrop tomatoes with lots of marigold but it works a bit less good than rotation.
Signet marigolds ( Tagetes tenuifolia ) do not work.
Also note that marigold attracts thrips.
Root knot nematodes only live in the soil and in or on the roots.

Sterilize soil in nurseries by burning lots of dry wood rests and plant material on the seedbed and incorporating the hot material into the soil.; Incorporate dry chopped plants of wild marigolds (Tagetes) into the seedbed (be aware that fresh wild marigold can inhibit germination); Alternatively remove the topsoil of seedbeds and replace with fresh compost.
Grow fallow during the off-season, for example for livestock feeding.
Plough directly after harvest and prior to the fallow season to expose nematodes to drying.
Monitoring: Root knot nematodes are very small worms that cannot be seen with the naked eye.
Search for plants that appear entirely weakened, and may even become yellowed and/or remain small.
The plants often entirely wilt during warm weather.

Pull out some of these plants to search for pearl- like swellings (also called knots, or galls) on roots wherein nematodes live. (note that this is a typical nematode symptom in tomatoes, but such swellings in legumes are normal and not nematodes)
In case that about 1/4th to 1/3rd of the plants are infected in the field, actions should be considered.
Direct Control: It is easier to prevent nematode mass occurrence than to control it.
For small plots, incorporation of neem seed cake or powder into the soil (1 kg per 10 m2) can help to reduce root knot nematode populations.
Make a 2 to 3 cropping cycle break with nematode-non- susceptible crops.
Restrictions: Synthetic nematicides do exist, but they are not very effective and often highly toxic to farmers, consumers and the environment.
Chemical fumigation of soils is not allowed in
IPM because being highly toxic to the soil environment.

Always consult recent list of registered pesticides (MAFC / TPRI).
